newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CORDOVA PITCHES TWO-HIT SHUTOUT AS PIRATES END SKID.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CORDOVA PITCHES TWO-HIT SHUTOUT AS PIRATES END SKID.

text.p: Francisco Cordova pitched the game of his career and Jermaine Allensworth made an immediate impact on his return from the disabled list to help the Pittsburgh Pirates halt a six-game slide on Monday.

Cordova (6-5) pitched a two-hit shutout, allowing only two runners to get as far as second base, while Allensworth provided a comfortable cushion for Cordova with a bases-loaded triple as the Pirates blanked the Houston Astros 6-0.
Cordova walked two and struck out in the low-hit outing of his career.
"I had good command of my pitches tonight and was able to locate the ball," Cordova said of his second career shutout. "Tonight I dominated the hitters."

Allensworth was activated before the game after spending five weeks on the DL with a broken left hand. His three-run triple highlighted a five-run eighth that broke open a duel between Cordova and Ramon Garcia (3-5).
But Jose Guillen's solo homer with two out in the top of the fifth was all the offence the Cordova needed.
Garcia allowed three runs and five hits in seven-plus innings, while striking out nine in a losing effort as the Astros saw their three-game winning streak end.
"We ran into a guy you can't hit," Astros manager Larry Dierker said. "That's the best way to stop any streak."
In San Francisco, Steve Finley homered three times for the second time this year and Tony Gwynn's double snapped a fifth-inning tie as the San Diego Padres beat the Giants 11-6.

Finley smacked one off Giants starter Mark Gardner in the third, another off Rich Rodriguez in the seventh and his third solo shot of the night off Joe Roa in the eighth. Wally Joyner added a three-run homer and a solo blast for San Diego as the Padres tied a team record with five round-trippers.
Jim Bruske (1-0) got the win in relief of Will Cunnane, scattering three hits and a walk over five shutout innings.
Mark Gardner (8-3) was bombed for seven runs and 12 hits in five innings for San Francisco.
In Montreal, Jim Bullinger fired a four-hitter for his second shutout of the season as the surging Expos blanked the Cincinnati Reds 5-0.
Bullinger (5-6) won for the third time in his last four starts with his fourth career shutout.
F.P. Santangelo extended his hitting streak to 18 games with a single in the second and hit a solo homer for Montreal, which has won 13 of its last 16 games.
John Smiley again got no offensive support and fell to 5-9 in losing his third straight decision. The Reds have scored two runs or less in nine of Smiley's 14 starts.
In New York, Rick Reed tossed a six-hitter, outdueling John Smoltz, and Carl Everett's two-run homer in the sixth inning lifted the Mets to a 3-2 win over the Atlanta Braves.
Reed (5-4) gave up two runs with just two walks and four strikeouts in a complete-game shutout.

Everett, who hit a three-run homer in the 10th inning to win Sunday's game against Pittsburgh, lined a 3-2 pitch from Smoltz (6-7) just over the right-field wall to score Todd Hundley and turn a 2-1 deficit into the Mets' fifth consecutive win.

In St Louis, rookie Jeremi Gonzalez pitched a four-hitter for his first career complete game and shutout and Mark Grace homered and drove in two runs as the Chicago Cubs stopped a five-game losing streak with a 3-0 victory over the Cardinals.
Gonzalez (3-2) walked one and struck out five in his sixth major-league start. He allowed only one runner to reach third and retired the last eight batters he faced.
Fernando Valenzuela (2-10) allowed three runs and five hits over six innings to become the first 10-game loser in the National League.
In Philadelphia, Scott Rolen knocked in five runs and Curt Schilling struck out a career-high 13 as the Phillies halted an eight-game skid with a 9-3 win over the Florida Marlins.
Rolen put the Phils in front in the bottom of the first with a two-run double off starter Rick Helling and widened the gap to 5-0 in the third with his eighth homer of the season.
Darren Daulton and Ruben Amaro added two-run homers for Philadelphia.
Schilling (9-6) allowed three runs and six hits in seven innings, while boosting his league-leading strikeout total to 139. Helling (2-5) was rocked for seven runs in four innings.
In Los Angeles, Hideo Nomo allowed five hits over eight innings and Eric Karros and Raul Mondesi homered in a five-run first inning to power the Dodgers to a 5-3 win over the Colorado Rockies.
Nomo (7-6), making his first start against the Rockies since tossing a no-hitter at Colorado last September 17, allowed three runs with three walks and five strikeouts.
Karros hit a two-run homer to give the Dodgers a 3-0 lead and Mondesi followed with a solo shot for a four-run cushion.
Colorado's Kevin Ritz (5-7) allowed five runs and eight hits in 6 1/3 innings to take the loss.
